title: Power and batteries (P = I x E)
idea: Power in watts is current times voltage. A battery's amp-hours divided by the current you draw tells you how long it lasts.

lines: Battery hours = amp-hours / average current draw

compare.how: Power, in watts. Memory hook: PIE.
Voltage, in volts. That is Ohm's law, a different formula.
How much a battery holds. Divide by average amps to get hours.

traps.why: Volts divided by amps gives ohms, not watts. Power multiplies: P = I x E.
That is 13.8 + 10. Power multiplies: 13.8 x 10 = 138 W.
That is 120 + 12. Current is power divided by voltage: 120 / 12 = 10 A.
Mobile rigs run on a car's 13.8 V system, not 24 V.
That is only about 55 W going in, and a transmitter turns some of it into heat. A 50 W rig needs about 12 A.

traps.wrong: Divide the watt-hour rating of the battery by the peak power consumption of the equipment
traps.why: Peak draw only happens some of the time. Use amp-hours divided by the average current.
